title: A break inside nested loops

curriculum.title: Inner Break in Nested Loops
curriculum.answer:
## Inner `break` keeps the outer loop going

An inner `break` exits the nearest inner loop. Any remaining statements in the current outer-loop body run next. Only after that body finishes does the outer loop advance to its next item. That pattern is useful when each inner list needs only one action, such as counting rows that contain a value.

```python
rooms = [[1, 2], [3, 4], [2, 9]]
wanted = 2
hits = 0
for room in rooms:
    for seat in room:
        if seat == wanted:
            hits = hits + 1
            break
print(hits)
```

```text
2
```

Walk the values: `room` is first `[1, 2]`. The inner loop checks `1`, then `2`. On `2` the test is true, `hits` becomes `1`, and `break` leaves the inner loop. Control returns to the outer loop, so `room` becomes `[3, 4]`. Neither item matches, so `hits` stays `1`. Finally `room` is `[2, 9]`; the first item matches, `hits` becomes `2`, and `break` stops that inner scan. Then `print` shows `2`.

```python
bags = [[5, 5], [6, 7]]
wanted = 5
total = 0
for bag in bags:
    for marble in bag:
        if marble == wanted:
            total = total + 1
            break
print(total)
```

```text
1
```

Here the first bag has two `5` values, but `total` grows only once because `break` skips the rest of that inner list. A common mistake is thinking `break` stops both loops. It does not: without an outer stop, later rows are still visited. Another mistake is forgetting `break`, so `[5, 5]` would add `2` instead of `1`. Checked attempts are not proof of durable mastery.

exercise.title: Count Boxes With Wanted Item
exercise.instructions: Count boxes that contain wanted. Inputs: boxes is a list of lists of numbers; wanted is one number. Use nested for loops and break the inner loop after the first match in a box so each box adds at most 1. Assign the count to hits. Example: boxes=[[1,2],[3,4]] and wanted=2 gives hits=1.

fresh_exercise.title: Count Trays With Mark
fresh_exercise.instructions: Count trays that contain mark. Inputs: trays is a list of lists of words; mark is one word. Scan each tray from left to right and count a tray once when mark is found, then stop that inner scan and continue with the next tray. Assign the count to found. Example: trays=[["a","b"],["c","a"]] and mark="a" gives found=2.
